title: How Indiana University turned audience connection into a championship-worthy social playbook
content:
Indiana University’s football team spent the 2025 season chasing—and winning-–a national championship. Behind the scenes, IU’s social media team spent it managing a Smart Inbox in Sprout Social that ballooned to more than five times its normal size almost overnight, while ramping up staff from across the university who had never touched the brand’s social inbox before.
Jill Trimbach, IU’s Executive Director of Social Media, was managing that growth in real time. On a normal week, her team runs publishing, inbox monitoring, keyword listening and reporting across IU’s flagship social media accounts. IU Football’s championship run turned that normal week into something else entirely.
In the final 36 seconds of IU’s game against Penn State, Omar Cooper Jr. made a catch that won the game. Minutes later, a message landed in IU’s inbox:
IU’s team could have scrolled past it. Instead, they wrote back. They kept in touch to ask how mom and baby were doing. The family, thrilled, sent baby photos and gave IU permission to share their story.
A producer from College GameDay on ESPN saw the post and reached out to Jill. The show went on to interview star players Fernando Mendoza and Omar Cooper Jr. alongside the new parents, pairing the players’ reaction to the winning catch with the family’s reaction to the baby’s arrival on national television.
That segment did not start with a media pitch. It started with someone on IU’s team choosing to reply to a message from a stranger with genuine care, because the inbox was manageable enough to notice a single, standout DM in the first place.
With the country’s eyes on IU Football and their newest fan, Jill’s team used the opportunity to show fans all that Indiana University offers.
The team tracked this shift in audience interest in real time with tags and social listening: a postseason content tag, tags for academic excellence and IU’s Indianapolis and regional campuses, and expanded Listening topics like #HeIsMendoza once quarterback Fernando Mendoza became a Heisman contender. IU even secured a billboard in Times Square for the night of the Heisman ceremony. To Jill and her team, Fernando was a great example of a student athlete who took his academic journey seriously, so they used this time to congratulate him and also leveraged the Heisman to also talk about their academic excellence — specifically the “excellence on and off the field” framing.
The strategy worked off-screen too. IU deployed new animated digital out-of-home signage on site for each game, then amplified that creative on social through Sprout Social — so the same message reached fans in the stadium and the much larger audience watching from everywhere else.
With the world watching, the social team carried that same strategy through a run of standout posts spotlighting IU beyond the scoreboard: fans repping IU at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway , Kirkwood Ave erupting in celebration , IU history and collections at the Peach Bowl.
The reach went beyond IU’s own channels, too. Months before the championship run, IU’s announcement that it had become the largest living alumni network was featured multiple times on The Pat McAfee Show, generating interest and traffic from the show’s audience on YouTube and across ESPN’s social channels.
None of the insights from these efforts stayed confined to the social team. Jill’s group reports on impressions, engagement rate and net audience growth from football content, and uses tagged data to show leadership how much of that audience also touched assets focused on academic and brand priorities, in addition to athletics. Together, this gave leadership irrefutable proof that the social team’s work during a high-pressure moment elevated IU’s brand, academic story and national visibility, not just its athletics program.
IU’s social team did not just survive a five-times increase in inbox volume. They created a playbook for how to scale social capabilities, showcase their brand and create authentic audience connections—and then used it to introduce the country to a fuller picture of all the university offers its students and alumni.
